topic_groups.topic: Public Health, Infectious Disease and Policy

articles.title: Drug decriminalization in BC reduced police encounters for drug possession, with no changes in drug-related deaths
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research in the Canadian Medical Association Journal found British Columbia's drug decriminalization policy was associated with fewer police encounters for drug possession. The analysis did not detect changes in drug toxicity deaths or drug-related hospitalizations linked to decriminalization or later partial recriminalization.

articles.title: New US Medicare pricing policies could reshape global pharmaceutical markets
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Lancet modeling study examined how a U.S. Medicare Most-Favored-Nation pricing policy could affect international drug markets. The model suggests manufacturers may respond by raising prices or delaying launches in other high-income countries when those prices influence Medicare payments.

articles.title: Third measles death recorded in US in 2026
articles.summary_3_sentences: Authorities reported that a 40-year-old woman in Pennsylvania died of measles, bringing the U.S. death toll for 2026 to three. The report links the event to concern about declining vaccination rates for a preventable infectious disease.

articles.title: DR Congo's worst Ebola epidemic ever passes 7,000 cases
articles.summary_3_sentences: Congolese authorities reported that the Democratic Republic of Congo's worst Ebola outbreak has surpassed 7,000 cases. The article describes the continuing scale of the epidemic rather than a new treatment finding.

articles.title: River Swimming May Raise Risk of Skin Problems
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that swimming in rivers and lakes may be associated with a higher risk of skin ailments. The visible summary does not specify the exact skin conditions or establish causality.

articles.title: Fallowed Farms Linked to Valley Fever Spikes
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Science Advances study examined how land-use shifts in California may influence valley fever patterns. The report focuses on links between fallowed farms and spikes in valley fever, a fungal disease affected by environmental conditions.

articles.title: Training nurses like athletes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The University of Texas at Arlington is introducing a nursing education approach that treats nurses as clinical athletes. The article describes the program through a nursing student's experience and frames it as an innovation in clinical training.

articles.title: First-line trastuzumab deruxtecan significantly improves progression-free survival in HER2-mutant lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: Primary phase 3 DESTINY-Lung04 results found first-line trastuzumab deruxtecan improved progression-free survival compared with pembrolizumab plus platinum chemotherapy in advanced or metastatic HER2-mutant NSCLC. The findings were presented at the IASLC 2026 World Conference on Lung Cancer.

articles.title: Update shows sustained overall survival benefit with adjuvant osimertinib in resected EGFR-mutated lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: An exploratory 8-year landmark update from the phase 3 ADAURA trial reported continued overall survival benefit with adjuvant osimertinib. The analysis involved patients with completely resected EGFR-mutated stage IB-IIIA NSCLC.

articles.title: Zidesamtinib demonstrates 93% response rate in ROS1-positive lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The global phase 1/2 ARROS-1 trial reported clinically meaningful activity for zidesamtinib in advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC. The reported findings focused on patients who had not previously received a tyrosine kinase inhibitor.

articles.title: Amivantamab-chemotherapy demonstrates longest overall survival reported for lung cancer with EGFR mutation
articles.summary_3_sentences: Phase 3 PAPILLON results found first-line amivantamab plus carboplatin-pemetrexed was associated with numerically longer overall survival than chemotherapy alone. The study involved previously untreated advanced NSCLC with EGFR exon 20 insertion mutations.

articles.title: Trial supports MRI surveillance over preventive brain radiation in small-cell lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The international phase 3 SWOG S1827 MAVERICK trial found MRI surveillance alone improved cognitive failure-free survival compared with MRI surveillance plus prophylactic cranial irradiation. The findings concern patients with small-cell lung cancer and were presented at WCLC.

articles.title: Trial shows risvutatug rezetecan significantly improves overall survival in relapsed small-cell lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The randomized phase 3 ARTEMIS-008 trial found risvutatug rezetecan improved overall survival compared with topotecan in relapsed small-cell lung cancer. The antibody-drug conjugate targets B7-H3 and was studied after progression on or after platinum-based chemotherapy.

articles.title: Combination therapy does not meet primary endpoints in first-line PD-L1-high metastatic non-small cell lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The phase 3 EVOKE-03/KEYNOTE-D46 trial found sacituzumab govitecan plus pembrolizumab did not significantly improve progression-free survival compared with pembrolizumab alone. The study involved first-line treatment of metastatic NSCLC with PD-L1 tumor proportion score of 50% or greater.

articles.title: Tam-Peli extends survival by nearly four months in relapsed small-cell lung cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The phase 3 TAISHAN-302 trial reported that tambotatug pelitecan improved overall survival, progression-free survival and objective response rate compared with topotecan. The B7-H3 antibody-drug conjugate was studied in relapsed small-cell lung cancer.

articles.title: FDA Expands Hyrnuo Use in HER2-Mutated Lung Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The FDA expanded the indication for Bayer's sevabertinib, marketed as Hyrnuo, for a rare HER2-mutated subtype of non-small-cell lung cancer. The visible summary describes a regulatory expansion but does not provide response rates or safety details.

topic_groups.topic: Cancer Biology, Screening and Personalized Oncology

articles.title: New analysis points to low overdiagnosis in breast cancer screening
articles.summary_3_sentences: A new analysis addresses overdiagnosis in breast cancer screening, the detection of cancers that would not have caused symptoms during a woman's lifetime. The title indicates the analysis points to low overdiagnosis, though the provided summary does not include numerical estimates.

articles.title: Pancreatic tumors use clotting pathway to build immune shields, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers at the Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai found that small populations of pancreatic cancer cells can create localized immune-protective niches. The study links a clotting pathway to tumor immune shielding and may inform future immunotherapy research.

articles.title: Moderna and Merck's Cancer Vaccine Passes Phase 3 Test
articles.summary_3_sentences: Moderna and Merck announced that a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine passed a phase 3 test. The visible article text does not provide efficacy measurements, safety results or the cancer indication.

articles.title: AI virtual cell uses protein dynamics to predict personalized breast cancer treatments
articles.summary_3_sentences: An AI tool called ProteinTalks was developed to predict whether drugs may work against breast cancer cell lines. The tool uses protein dynamics to identify potential drug combinations and proteins linked to drug resistance.

articles.title: Cancer Metabolism Drives Immune Suppression in Triple Negative Breast Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines how metabolic reactions in cancer cells may drive immune suppression in triple-negative breast cancer. The visible summary links cancer metabolism with tumor immune effects but does not provide detailed experimental results.

articles.title: Bacteria in the Urinary Tract Found to Produce Testosterone
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that bacteria in the urinary tract can produce testosterone. The article frames the finding as relevant to prostate cancer because androgen hormones can support disease progression.

articles.title: Experimental drug targets "undruggable" cancer protein
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental therapeutic was reported to disrupt MYC, a cancer protein often described as difficult to drug. The findings were described in preclinical models, where the drug reduced MYC-driven tumor growth.

articles.title: Personalized Cancer Vaccine Shows Protects from Melanoma Recurrence
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on a personalized cancer vaccine being studied for protection against melanoma recurrence. It describes a Merck and Moderna collaboration, but the visible summary does not provide trial design, efficacy or safety details.

articles.title: Colorectal Cancer Damages Nerves
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that colorectal cancer can damage nerves. The visible summary discusses this in the broader context of cancer progression and treatment approaches, without providing detailed mechanisms or study design.

articles.title: Aging oxidation drives brain proteins into harmful condensates, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in Nature Structural & Molecular Biology described how sulfenylation and persulfidation regulate key brain proteins during aging. The work links age-related oxidation chemistry to harmful protein condensates, but the provided summary does not specify clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Masked antibodies may open intracellular treatment route for Parkinson's disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses masked antibodies as a possible route to target intracellular disease mechanisms in Parkinson's disease. The summary emphasizes the general limitation that conventional antibodies have difficulty entering cells.

articles.title: Rare cortical neurons can synchronize brain activity and promote sleep in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in mice found that rare cortical neurons can synchronize brain activity and promote sleep. The finding challenges the view that the cerebral cortex is mainly a passive follower of deeper sleep-wake control regions.

articles.title: Want to lower your risk of dementia? It doesn't involve a blood test
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article notes that blood tests that may predict Alzheimer's disease years before symptoms are not yet fully ready for routine use. It emphasizes that people can still pursue dementia risk-reduction strategies without first taking a blood test.

articles.title: Lifestyle Intervention Boosts Cognition in Older Adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: A structured lifestyle program was given to older adults at risk of dementia. Participants showed measurable improvements in memory and executive function after the intervention, according to cognitive assessments.

articles.title: Early Statin Use Tied to Lower Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Starting statins within one year of a type 2 diabetes diagnosis was associated with a 15% lower relative risk of dementia. The visible summary describes an association and does not establish that statins caused the risk reduction.

articles.title: AI platform identifies potential Alzheimer's drug targets
articles.summary_3_sentences: An artificial intelligence platform screened genomic and multi-omics data to identify potential Alzheimer's disease drug targets. Five genes were highlighted as candidates, with validation experiments planned to assess druggability.

articles.title: Ultra-fast microscope design captures zebrafish brain seizures
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists developed an ultra-fast volumetric microscope to image zebrafish brains. The system recorded three-dimensional seizure propagation in real time, providing a tool for studying neuronal seizure dynamics in this model.

articles.title: Sleep Disruptions Linked to Genetic Alzheimer's Disease Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers reported that frequent micro-awakenings correlate with genetic risk for Alzheimer's disease. Sleep fragmentation was measured using actigraphy, and the findings suggest sleep quality may be an early marker of susceptibility rather than proof of causation.

articles.title: HEPA Air Purifiers May Boost Cognition After Age 40
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adults aged 40 and older used HEPA air purifiers at home for one month in the reported study. Cognitive testing showed a 12% improvement after the intervention, with the proposed mechanism involving reduced indoor pollutants.

articles.title: Human brain organoids gain sense of time and space
articles.summary_3_sentences: Two recent studies advanced research on human brain organoids. The visible summary reports that one study found organoids can record the passage of time, while the broader work examined representations of time and space in organoid models.

articles.title: High-Dose Vitamin D Linked to Better Cognition
articles.summary_3_sentences: Daily vitamin D intake of at least 5,000 IU was linked to better cognitive scores in older adults. The visible summary describes an association and does not establish that high-dose vitamin D caused the cognitive differences.

articles.title: Speaking Multiple Languages May Slow Brain Aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: Speaking multiple languages was associated with slower brain aging. The visible summary frames this as an observed relationship rather than a causal finding.

articles.title: Shingles Vaccine Linked to 24% Lower Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Older adults who received the Shingrix shingles vaccine had a 24% lower observed risk of being diagnosed with dementia within four years. The article reports an association between vaccination and dementia diagnosis risk.

articles.title: Estrogen Therapy Linked to Lower Dementia Risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: Later-life use of estrogen-only hormone therapy was associated with 39% lower odds of a clinical dementia diagnosis. The visible summary reports an association and does not establish a causal protective effect.

articles.title: Study suggests profile of people diagnosed with ADHD and autism has changed over the past decade
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study led by ISGlobal and Aarhus University found that children and adolescents diagnosed with ADHD or autism in Denmark now share more characteristics with peers in the general population than those diagnosed a decade ago. The finding suggests diagnostic profiles have shifted over time.

articles.title: Ketamine reveals shifting brain activity patterns linked to depression improvement in older adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified time-specific brain activity patterns after ketamine treatment in older adults with treatment-resistant depression. The article links these changing activity patterns with depression improvement, without providing detailed response rates in the visible summary.

articles.title: Ketamine Shows Promise for Bipolar Depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: Ketamine infusions may help ease treatment-resistant bipolar depression. The visible summary does not provide response rates, treatment schedule or duration of benefit.

articles.title: IBD Linked to Higher Risk of Psychiatric Disorders
articles.summary_3_sentences: Patients with inflammatory bowel disease were reported to have increased incidence of psychiatric conditions. The risk elevation appeared two to three years after IBD diagnosis in a cohort analysis adjusted for age, sex and comorbidities.

articles.title: Early Social Media Use Linked to Anxiety, Depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: An analysis found that earlier first access to social media platforms was associated with higher anxiety and depressive symptoms. The reported survey analysis controlled for socioeconomic status and screen time.

articles.title: Simple Daily Routine May Improve Sleep, Depression, Heart Health, and More
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers examined the health effects of maintaining a consistent daily schedule. Participants who kept regular sleep, meal and activity times showed improvements in sleep quality, mood and cardiovascular markers over eight weeks.

articles.title: Ozempic Shows Promise in Bipolar Disorder
articles.summary_3_sentences: Semaglutide, known as Ozempic and Wegovy, was linked with a lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization in people with bipolar disorder. The visible summary reports this hospitalization-related association but does not establish causality.

articles.title: VR and Scents Boost Mental Health in Isolated Space
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Frontiers in Psychology study examined mental health support in isolated space-like settings. It explored whether virtual reality nature scenes and scents could help astronauts maintain well-being.

articles.title: PlaySmart Game Boosts Teen Mental Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A JAMA Network Open study examined whether the PlaySmart video game could help treat teen depression. The visible summary presents the game as a potential mental health intervention but does not provide effect sizes.

articles.title: Daily Fruit Juice Reduces Symptoms of Depression
articles.summary_3_sentences: Adding a daily glass of 100% fruit juice or a smoothie to a diet rich in fruits and vegetables was reported to lower depressive symptoms. The article describes the dietary intervention but does not provide detailed study design information in the visible summary.

topic_groups.topic: Cardiometabolic, Obesity, Respiratory and Lifestyle Health

articles.title: Protein restriction may trigger body-wide program linked to longer life
articles.summary_3_sentences: A perspective from LSU's Pennington Biomedical Research Center proposes that dietary protein restriction may promote healthy aging through a coordinated physiological response. The proposed framework connects cellular nutrient sensing with hormones, the brain and body-wide changes.

articles.title: Early blood protein clues could identify children at risk of cardiometabolic disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified early blood protein signals of cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic disease in children as young as 8 years old. The article notes these early signs may be reversible with a class of weight-loss drugs widely used by adults, but does not provide intervention results in the summary.

articles.title: A Drug That Burns Calories Leaves Brown Fat Untouched
articles.summary_3_sentences: Selective beta2 adrenergic receptor stimulation increased whole-body energy expenditure without activating brown fat. The report suggests calorie-burning effects can occur independently of brown-fat activation.

articles.title: Wegovy Shows Promise for Younger Children With Obesity
articles.summary_3_sentences: A phase 3 trial found Wegovy, also known as semaglutide, helped more than 40% of younger children with obesity fall below the clinical threshold. The visible text does not specify duration, comparator or safety findings.

articles.title: Peppermint Oil Lowers Blood Pressure
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that peppermint oil may lower blood pressure and describes it as a possible treatment approach. The visible excerpt does not provide study design, effect size or safety details.

articles.title: Semaglutide Linked to Fewer Asthma Attacks
articles.summary_3_sentences: Semaglutide use was linked to an almost 40% reduction in asthma attacks. The visible excerpt describes an association and does not provide study-design details or establish causation.

articles.title: Sprinting Offers Unique Benefits Over Moderate Exercise
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article compares intense exercise with moderate exercise and reports that sprinting may provide unique health benefits. The visible summary highlights exercise intensity as an important factor but does not provide specific outcomes.

articles.title: Nightly Pill Reduces Sleep Apnea Breathing Interruptions
articles.summary_3_sentences: A phase 3 trial evaluated a nightly oral medication for obstructive sleep apnea. The pill reduced breathing interruptions by about 44% compared with placebo over 12 weeks, with events monitored by polysomnography.

articles.title: Hypothyroidism Linked to Higher Risk of Sleep Apnea
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that people with hypothyroidism had a higher likelihood of obstructive sleep apnea than matched controls. The authors suggested clinicians consider sleep apnea screening in patients with hypothyroidism.

articles.title: Coffee May Improve Many Aspects of Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports possible health benefits of coffee involving heart health, metabolism and body composition. The visible summary does not specify study design or quantify the reported effects.

articles.title: Type 1 Diabetes Helped with Fasting, not Calorie Counting
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Diabetes Care study examined intermittent fasting compared with calorie counting in people with type 1 diabetes. The visible summary reports that fasting may help, but does not provide detailed outcome measures or safety information.

articles.title: Shedding new light on DNA repair in early human embryos, with implications for gene editing
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature study examined how early human embryos repair DNA damage caused during gene editing. The work is framed as relevant to the safety and limitations of possible future embryo gene-correction approaches.

articles.title: Immune Cells Starve the Aging Placenta of NAD+
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature Communications report examined inflammatory aging of the placenta in women of older gestational age. It found that immune cells can reduce NAD+ availability in the aging placenta.

articles.title: Study reveals a protein that could predict preeclampsia
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study identified low levels of the placental protein isthmin-2, or ISM2, as a potential predictor of preeclampsia. Low ISM2 levels were also associated with fetal growth restriction.

articles.title: Maternal Immune Activation Alters Gene Expression in Fetus
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines how maternal immune activation affects fetal development. It reports changes in fetal gene expression linked to immune activity during pregnancy.

articles.title: New Placental Atlas Links Genetics and Cannabis to Pregnancy Complications
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Nature placental atlas provides single-cell spatial resolution of the placental interface. The work reports associations between genetic variants, cannabis exposure and pregnancy complications.

articles.title: The Gut Microbiome Impacts Uterine Inflammation and Female Reproductive Health
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Journal of Advanced Research study examined links between the gut microbiome and uterine inflammation. It found that maternal gut dysbiosis increases uterine inflammation, connecting microbiome changes with female reproductive health.

topic_groups.topic: Microbiome, UTI and Gastrointestinal or Oral Health

articles.title: Dynamic UTI model transforms bacterial behavior
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers at University College London developed a model of urinary tract infection intended to better recapitulate human biology. The model is aimed at studying bacterial behavior during UTIs, though the visible excerpt does not provide specific measurements.

articles.title: Novel Model Provides Insights into Recurrent UTIs
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses a novel model for studying recurrent urinary tract infections. It notes that UTIs are among the most common infections worldwide, with more than 350 million cases each year.

articles.title: Link between IBS-C and Gut Microbiome Metabolites
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article describes a 2020 study identifying two gut microbiome metabolites altered in people with irritable bowel syndrome with constipation. It frames these metabolites as measurable differences related to IBS-C.

articles.title: Omega-3 and Aspirin Rival Antibiotics for Gum Disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: Omega-3 combined with low-dose aspirin performed similarly to antibiotics in patients with severe gum disease. The article reports comparable performance in advanced periodontal disease rather than superiority over antibiotics.

articles.title: Smartphones could be used to screen for cataracts and other eye problems
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found strong agreement between cataract referral decisions based on remotely reviewed smartphone images and in-person ophthalmologist exams. The study was conducted in the context of rural eye camps.

articles.title: Simple perception test can accurately predict success of laser surgery for age-related vision loss
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that a simple perception test can predict success of laser blended vision surgery for presbyopia. The procedure corrects one eye for distance and the other for near vision, requiring the brain to coordinate both eyes.

articles.title: New research reveals underlying mechanisms of eye inflammation
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in The American Journal of Pathology found evidence that immune cells enter the retina through the body's standard pathway. The research identifies PECAM as a gatekeeper and neutrophils as proresolving mediators in eye inflammation.

articles.title: Cialis Linked to Higher Glaucoma Risk in Men
articles.summary_3_sentences: Men taking tadalafil, also known as Cialis, were reported to have a higher risk of glaucoma and other eye-pressure problems. The visible summary describes an association and does not provide the size of the risk increase or prove causation.

articles.title: Antihistamines May Offer Little Relief for Eczema
articles.summary_3_sentences: Oral antihistamines added to existing eczema treatments were reported to be unlikely to meaningfully reduce eczema or itch severity. The visible text does not provide participant numbers or effect sizes.

articles.title: AstraZeneca and Amgen's Tezspire Completes a Successful Late-Stage Trial
articles.summary_3_sentences: AstraZeneca and Amgen's Tezspire met all objectives in a phase 3 study involving eosinophilic esophagitis. The visible excerpt identifies the trial as late-stage but does not provide detailed efficacy or safety results.

articles.title: Peptides from scorpion venom could help fight liver disease
articles.summary_3_sentences: A review reports that scorpion venom may contain peptides relevant to inflammation and liver disease. The finding is presented as a potential therapeutic direction, not a confirmed treatment effect.

articles.title: Engineered Antibodies Provide Protection Against Cobra Toxin
articles.summary_3_sentences: Engineered antibodies were studied for protection against cobra toxin. The visible summary frames the work in the context of tropical disease but does not provide details on experimental model or outcome measures.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Sheds Light on How Our Immune System Functions
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports on the use of artificial intelligence to improve understanding of immune-system function. The visible summary is broad and does not describe a specific dataset or experimental result.

articles.title: A strict diet reduces genetic mutations in mice
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study in mice found that calorie restriction led to fewer DNA mutations as the animals aged. The reported result was observed in mice and should not be assumed to apply directly to humans.

articles.title: Actin Scaffold Acts as Gatekeeper for Muscle Membrane Growth
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Science Advances study examined regulation of skeletal muscle architecture. The research identified an actin scaffold that acts as a gatekeeper for muscle membrane growth.

articles.title: Satellite Cell Readiness is Governed by an RNA-Binding Protein in Muscle
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Stem Cell Reports study identified a role for the RNA-binding protein TDP-43 in muscle satellite cell readiness. The article reports that TDP-43 governs aspects of satellite cell preparedness but does not provide detailed mechanistic data in the visible summary.
